evidence: SIYI A8 mini spec page (siyi.biz/en/product/tri-axis-single-camera-gimbal/a8-mini/spec/); A8 mini User Manual v1.10 (2025-09) sections 1.3, 2.3.1, 5.3, 7.3.2; SIYI Gimbal Camera External SDK Protocol V0.1.1 (2025-02-26) commands 0x00-0x82 and Appendix 2
notes: Raw: images JPG only (manual 1.3). Metadata: EXIF time + GPS on photos only (manual 2.3.1); nothing per video frame. SDK streams gimbal attitude (0x0D/0x25), which is pose, not image metadata. ISP: white balance Auto only; no SDK command for exposure, WB, sharpness, contrast, saturation or denoise; HDR status readable (0x0A), HDR toggle 'not supported'. Encoding: SDK 0x20/0x21 read/set main and sub stream codec, resolution (1920x1080 or 1280x720) and fixed bitrate; recording codec fixed. A8 mini support for 0x20/0x21 is inferred from Appendix 2's note that unlisted TTL/UDP commands work on the whole series; A8 mini has no TCP support. uncompressed_out = partial and calibration = partial are inferred: HDMI is likely uncompressed but ISP-processed; digital zoom and stream-resolution switching change effective intrinsics. evidence: Sony IMX477-AACK-C datasheet E17203 (excerpt, 25 pages): Features, Device Structure, 6-5 Image Readout Operation, 6-6-1 Embedded Data Line control, Figure 26 spectral sensitivity; MIPI CSI-2 spec v1.3 11.1.2 and Table 9 (embedded data type 0x12), 11.4.4-11.4.5 (RAW10/12). Both PDFs supplied by Teyr, not stored here
notes: Verified at sensor level: RAW12/10/8 output over CSI-2; integration time and gain set over I2C (6-5); can send 2 embedded data lines of register contents after frame start (6-6-1). Sensor has no colour processing, so white balance, colour matrix, denoise and sharpening happen in the host ISP (Jetson or libcamera), which you control: lockable_isp and isp_access = yes are inferred from that. per_frame_metadata = partial: which registers go in the embedded lines is in Sony's Software reference manual (not public), and the host driver must capture those lines rather than drop them (unchecked). The datasheet's table of contents lists on-chip Defect Pixel Correction (6-8-1), so 'raw' may already have defect pixels corrected; that section is not in the excerpt. calibration = unknown: depends on the module's lens (e.g. interchangeable C/CS mount on some boards). COMP8 is a compressed option; use RAW10/12. Datasheet restricts use to consumer camcorders; check with the module vendor for other uses. Tier A holds only once a module and driver are chosen that keep raw output and embedded data.
